intro: Flexible meals are planned on purpose. “Cheat meals” become harmful when they mean secrecy, binge–restrict cycles, or moral licensing — not when they mean enjoying food you love inside an honest week.
buddyTip: Rename the idea: call it a planned enjoyment meal. Schedule it, log it, and keep the next meal normal.
mission: If you want a special meal this week, put it on the calendar, decide the outline, and commit to logging it without punishment.
why: All-or-nothing thinking creates underground eating. Honesty over Shame means special meals stay in the diary where Buddy can coach the week, not the fantasy week.

Energy balance cares about averages. A planned higher-calorie meal inside an otherwise consistent week is often compatible with goals. Unplanned weekend spirals plus Monday starvation usually are not.
Psychologically, forbidden foods gain power. Planned inclusion reduces the binge magnetism for many people.

what.lead: Healthy flexibility has rules of kindness.
points: Plan frequency that matches your goals — often one meal, not an unbound “cheat day”
Keep protein anchors on the same day when possible
Log the meal completely — including drinks
Review how you felt: satisfied vs out-of-control — adjust the plan

misconceptions.myth: A cheat day means the whole day is off and unlogged.
misconceptions.truth: Unbounded cheat days erase learning. Prefer a bounded meal with capture.

misconceptions.myth: If I’m serious, I never eat dessert again.
misconceptions.truth: Serious means sustainable. Inclusion skills are part of mastery.

steps: Choose the meal and roughly what you’ll order or cook
Eat normally earlier — arrive hungry, not starving
Enjoy without commentary that shames you or others
Log with Buddy the same day
Next meal: return to defaults (protein + plants)
Weekly review: did flexibility help adherence or trigger spirals?
how.buddyHelps: Buddy does not need a perfect week. Honest special meals improve coaching quality. Progress shows the week-level effect without moralising the slice of cake.

sections.title: When flexibility is not enough
paras: If planned meals regularly become binges, tighten structure, increase daytime protein/fibre, sleep more, and consider professional help for disordered patterns.
Buddy Academy coaches habits; clinical eating disorders need clinicians.

sections.title: Language matters
paras: “Cheat” implies crime. Try “planned meal,” “celebration meal,” or “flex meal.” Language shapes whether you hide or learn.

mistakes.quote: I earned this cheat because I was perfect for six days.
mistakes.why: Moral licensing increases extremes. Plan enjoyment without requiring perfection debt.

mistakes.quote: I won’t log it so it didn’t happen.
mistakes.why: It happened to your body. Let the diary stay honest.

mistakes.quote: After cheats I run a 1000-kcal day to compensate.
mistakes.why: Punishment drives the next binge. Resume maintenance of habits instead.

encouragement: You are allowed to enjoy food and still be consistent. Plan it, log it, continue — that is Progress over Perfection with dessert included.
